Leave-one-out cross-validation

Source: R/loo.R
loo.kb_fit.Rd

Estimate how well a fit predicts each observation when that observation is left out, by Pareto-smoothed importance-sampling leave-one-out cross-validation (PSIS-LOO; Vehtari et al. 2017).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'kb_fit'
loo(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A kb_fit object.

...

Passed to loo::loo(), for example cores.

Value

A psis_loo object from loo::loo().

Details

The pointwise results ($pointwise and loo::pareto_k_values()) have one row per observation, in the order of the fitted data. elpd_loo and the Pareto k diagnostic are described in kb_influence(), which adds them to the data. A Pareto k above the threshold in the printed result also marks the PSIS-LOO estimate as unreliable.

Use loo::loo_compare() to compare fits to the same data.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., and Gabry, J. (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing, 27, 1413-1432.

See also

log_lik() for the pointwise log-likelihood.

Other diagnostics: kb_converged(), kb_influence(), kb_plot_trace(), kb_sensitivity(), pp_check.kb_fit()

Examples

loo_weight <- loo(fit_weight_sim_nereo)
loo_weight
#> 
#> Computed from 1500 by 660 log-likelihood matrix.
#> 
#>          Estimate   SE
#> elpd_loo   -242.5 32.5
#> p_loo        30.3  1.8
#> looic       485.0 65.1
#> ------
#> MCSE of elpd_loo is 0.2.
#> MCSE and ESS estimates assume MCMC draws (r_eff in [0.7, 1.2]).
#> 
#> All Pareto k estimates are good (k < 0.69).
#> See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
loo::pareto_k_values(loo_weight)
